In build

Archie Mobile.

The app we are building for your phone.

Written and running here, not finished, and in neither app store.

What it is

Your computer, reachable from your pocket.

Your agent stays on the computer you installed it on, with your files and your connected accounts, and it keeps working there whether your phone is in your hand or face down on a table. The app is not running it. It reaches it.

Most of what you do at the desk you can do from here. What it cannot reach is what never leaves your computer: your passwords and keys, your knowledge files, and the rows inside a collection.

Sealed

Sealed before it leaves your computer.

Today your agent reaches you through a chat app, so what it tells you crosses that company’s servers. This does not. Your computer locks every message under a key it makes itself and hands to your phone by showing a code to scan. The key never passes through us.

So we hold the messages and cannot open them. “It never touches our servers” would be punchier and false. Your agent keeps working in the chat app you connected, too: this is a second door, not a replacement.

Side by side

Who can open what.

Each chat app Archie connects to, what that company publishes about encryption, and whether that company can open your agent’s messages, compared with the app Otian is building.
  What that company publishes Can they open it
Telegram An ordinary chat, which is the kind an agent uses, is not end to end. Telegram’s FAQ says cloud chats are “stored encrypted in the Telegram Cloud”, and that “several court orders from different jurisdictions are required to force us to give up any data”. Its end-to-end kind, a Secret Chat, is between two people and is not something an agent can useSource 1 Yes
Discord Every voice and video call is end-to-end encrypted. Text is not, in Discord’s own words: “We have no current plans to extend E2EE to text messages”Source 2 Yes
Slack “In Slack, customer data is encrypted at rest and in transit by default.” Archie joins as an ordinary bot, so your agent’s messages sit in that workspace like every other message in itSource 3 Yes
Matrix A Matrix room can be end-to-end encrypted. Archie cannot read one that is, so our connect guide asks for a room with encryption off. The same trade as the others, and it is our limitation rather than Matrix’sSource 4 Yes
iMessage on a Mac The exception. Apple encrypts it end to end and says “no one else can access your end-to-end encrypted data, not even Apple”. Archie reads it out of the Messages app on your own computer rather than over the networkSource 5 No
The app we are building Sealed on your computer before it leaves, under a key it gives your phone by camera. We hold the sealed messages and have no keySource 6 No, and neither can we
The catch

What sealing does not do.

What we can still see

Three things about each message are not sealed, because something has to read them without a key: when it was left, which version of Archie wrote it, and whether an instruction is waiting, finished or failed. So we can see that a phone is talking to a computer, and roughly when. Never what it said.

Whoever holds the phone holds the key

Sealing protects the message in the middle. It cannot protect you from a phone somebody else is holding. The fix is on your computer: unpair that phone, and its key retires with it, so nothing sent afterwards can be opened by it.

Where it stands

Honestly: not finished.

The app is written and it runs. The piece it needs on our side is not switched on, and it is in neither app store, so we cannot give you a date and will not invent one. Nothing about your setup has to change to be ready for it.

Sources for every claim on this page
1Telegram, on cloud chats and Secret Chats

“Secret chats use end-to-end encryption” while “Cloud Chats use client-server/server-client encryption and are stored encrypted in the Telegram Cloud”, and “several court orders from different jurisdictions are required to force us to give up any data”. From the Telegram FAQ, read on September 11, 2026.

2Discord, on what its encryption covers

Discord’s DAVE protocol covers “every voice and video call on Discord, whether in DMs, group DMs, voice channels, or Go Live streams”, and on text: “We have no current plans to extend E2EE to text messages.” From Discord’s own announcement, read on September 11, 2026.

3Slack, on encryption

“In Slack, customer data is encrypted at rest and in transit by default.” From Slack’s security page, read on September 11, 2026.

4Matrix, and our own limitation

This row is about Archie, not about Matrix. Our connection cannot read an encrypted room, so the connect guide asks for one with encryption off. Matrix supports end-to-end encryption well; the shortfall is ours.

5Apple, on iMessage

“No one else can access your end-to-end encrypted data, not even Apple.” From Apple’s iCloud data security overview, read on September 11, 2026. One caveat Apple states on the same page and we will not leave out: Messages in iCloud is end-to-end encrypted when iCloud Backup is off, so if you keep iCloud Backup on, check how Apple describes that before relying on it.

6Our side of the table

The sealed mailbox already exists and already carries phone access: what we hold and what we cannot open is on the Trust page, each line pointing at the code behind it. Messages are sealed with AES-256-GCM, an ordinary published cipher rather than anything of our own invention, and the key travels in the part of a web address browsers never send to a server.

What we have not claimed

Nothing here says Telegram, Discord or Slack read your messages. It says what each publishes about what it can do, and links their words so you can check ours. Nothing here says a chat app is unsafe: your agent works there today and we built those connections on purpose. And nothing claims to be the most secure anything: we have described one mechanism and shown you where it fails.

Next

Reaching your agent already works.

You do not have to wait for this. Connecting a chat app takes a few minutes and is the last step of setting an agent up: How It Works walks through it. The full list of what we hold is on the Trust page.
